o1.biggest_strength: The 'our biggest leak is not Semrush' section does the arithmetic the owner asked for: Lite is 44% of customers but 70% of monthly churn, usage-limit exits alone are 32% of all churn, and only 37% of a Lite cohort survives a year.
o1.biggest_mistake: Move 5 is 'do more content' with a study-to-trial-to-paid link that cannot be attributed, exactly the generic advice the owner flagged as annoying, and the header invents a 'November 2026' date the brief never gave.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Swap move 5 for a fourth data-backed product or lifecycle move (or drop to four moves) and stop inventing a report date.

o2.biggest_strength: It decides on page one: lose/tie/win/not-a-Semrush-problem, then 'do first this month', 'stop' and 'don't spend on', with every number traceable to the brief and the working shown.
o2.biggest_mistake: Move 5 partly recycles moves 1 and 3 (the report plus the multi-site test) instead of standing alone, and its '590 more paid accounts' assumes all 21,000 multi-site accounts convert at the test rate.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Make move 5 a standalone, sized bet with its own owner, milestone and kill criteria so it earns its slot as a separate move.

reason: Both nail where we lose (agencies on reporting and PPC) and that Lite limits are self-inflicted churn, but output 2 puts the decision on the first screen and gives a genuinely new move (a free Monday report inside Webmaster Tools) with its risk named, while output 1 spends its fifth slot on 'do more content' and dates the memo with an invented month.
